from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES', len(r.pages))
texts = []
for i, page in enumerate(r.pages, 1):
    text = f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n' + page.extract_text()
    texts.append(text)
    (p / f'page-{i}.txt').write_text(text)
(p / 'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:4]))

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from fractions import Fraction as F
P = [[F(1,10),F(9,10)],[F(9,10),F(1,10)]]
nu = [F(1),F(1)]
xi = [sum(nu[i]*P[i][j] for i in range(2)) for j in range(2)]
rho = [nu[i]+xi[i] for i in range(2)]
pi = [x / sum(rho) for x in rho]
K = [[P[i][j]/rho[j] for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
delta=[F(1),F(-1)]
quad = sum(delta[i]*K[i][j]*delta[j] for i in range(2) for j in range(2))
diff = sum((P[0][j]-P[1][j])**2/pi[j] for j in range(2))
print('A connected, aperiodic example with P = [[0.1,0.9],[0.9,0.1]], nu = [1,1]:')
print('stationary pi:',pi)
print('Eq. 6 diffusion distance squared:', diff, '=', float(diff))
print('Eq. 7 kernel quadratic form at t=1:', quad, '=', float(quad))
print('Correct stationary-weighted feature is P"'^t D_pi''^(-1/2); row K uses D_rho''^(-1).'"')
print('Full measure grid size:', 11*11*101)
PY"

strengths: Significance: Clustering digraphs without strong connectivity is a useful problem. With a well-defined transition matrix and strictly positive vertex measure, Eq. (4) provides a reversible walk that can connect distinct strongly connected components without teleportation, provided the underlying undirected support is connected.

Empirical promise: Evaluation covers 11 UCI datasets and four networks. Importantly, Appendix A.3 includes label-free parameter selection for a simplified variant: Table 4 reports average NMI of 63.45 versus 60.01 for PIC. These results provide some evidence beyond ground-truth-optimal tuning.

Presentation: The progression from graph operators to diffusion embeddings and practical clustering is easy to follow. Algorithms 1–2, parameter grids, dataset sizes, and supplementary derivations provide a useful implementation outline.
Research ethics: The experiments use established public benchmarks, and no material ethical concern is apparent from the manuscript.
weaknesses: Soundness—central kernel identity: Eqs. (6)–(7) are inconsistent. For a reversible walk Q with stationary distribution π, the defining diffusion distance has Gram matrix Q^t diag(π)^{-1}(Q^t)^T = Q^{2t} diag(π)^{-1}; Eq. (7) instead uses Q^t diag(ν+ξ)^{-1}. Beyond the normalization discrepancy, the missing factor of two can produce negative purported squared distances. For P=[[0.1,0.9],[0.9,0.1]], ν=(1,1), and t=1, Eq. (7) yields -0.8 between the two vertices, whereas the defining squared distance is 2.56. Furthermore, applying ordinary k-means to rows of K in Algorithm 1 uses the geometry of KK^T, not K. The implemented embedding therefore lacks the claimed diffusion-distance justification.

Soundness—scope and assumptions: The unrestricted applicability claim is too broad. Self-adjointness and aperiodicity do not establish irreducibility when the underlying support is disconnected. Moreover, Eqs. (4) and (9) require handling zero vertex measures and zero in/out-degrees; Eq. (8) does not always produce strictly positive measures at the permitted parameter endpoints. These cases matter for the non-strongly-connected digraphs motivating the paper and need explicit conventions or restrictions.

Evaluation: Section 6.1 selects parameters for agreement with ground truth and reports the best score over 100 restarts, without describing an independent validation protocol or reporting variability. The proposed method also receives a substantially larger parameter search than most baselines. Thus Tables 1–2 principally establish oracle performance. The appendix partially addresses this issue, but evaluates a reduced parameterization with joint CH/DCH selection; it does not validate the full method's assumption that a diffusion time selected using ν=1 transfers appropriately to a different vertex measure.

Originality and attribution of gains: The proposed walk follows directly from the generalized Laplacian already attributed to Sevi et al. (2022), while the corrected diffusion-kernel identity is standard Gram-matrix algebra. A useful contribution could still arise from combining these ingredients, but there is no comparison against generalized spectral clustering using the same vertex measure. Nor do the experiments isolate the effects of vertex weighting, diffusion filtering, and time selection. Since Eq. (4) itself symmetrizes weighted flows, controlled evidence is particularly needed to establish the claimed advantage in retaining useful directional information.

Reproducibility: The manuscript provides no code link and leaves feature preprocessing, random seeds, and the restart-selection objective insufficiently specified. There are concrete inconsistencies: Section 6.1 states an RSC grid of {1,...,20}, while Table 2 reports parameters such as 0.2 and 2.5. Appendix A.2 also changes the transition operator and its stationary measure without explicitly specifying the corresponding kernel normalization. These ambiguities prevent confident reconstruction of the reported results.

Significance and limitations: Avoiding eigendecomposition does not establish computational efficiency. Algorithm 1 constructs an N-by-N embedding, and matrix powers can become dense, requiring quadratic storage. No runtime, memory, or complexity comparison is provided, and all evaluated graphs have at most 2,485 vertices. The practical limitations of this computation, the required known cluster count, and the heuristic scale-selection procedure receive insufficient discussion.
